In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

socialization and social studies teacher education should be used to inculcate values, attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors that are consistent with the goals of social studies, including critical thinking, and with the goals of democracy, including tolerance of divergent viewpoints.

social studies teacher educators should seek to inculcates specific values, attitudes and beliefs in their K-12 students when the socializing purpose is more important than the purpose of developing critical thinkers.

social studies teacher educators should promote critical thinking in their students, but should also seek to socialize them in certain circumstances, including when the subject matter is particularly controversial, when students are not yet ready for critical thinking, and when social studies teacher educators are seeking to prepare students for teaching in K-12 schools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
socialization should be used when it is likely to be effective, but that it should be used only when it is likely that it will be effective.
the socialization of students is a worthy goal in social studies, but only when it is used to promote critical thinking, and when the socialization occurs within a context of critical thinking.

we should socialize students for shared values, attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors when we can do so in ways that are consistent with the goals of critical thinking and that promote democratic values and practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

social studies teacher educators should be explicit about the socialization goals they are pursuing in their courses, and they should be explicit about how their pedagogy supports or undermines those goals.

socialization and critical thinking need not be mutually exclusive, but that socializing for critical thinking and socializing for shared beliefs can be done in different ways, and at different times.
teacher educators must be aware of the socializing effects of their teaching, and must make conscious decisions about when and how to use socialization.
